mission_10: Hardware-Model Co-Design simultaneously optimizes both the neural network architecture and the hardware accelerator, finding pairs that achieve the best performance-energy trade-offs. Unlike hardware-aware NAS (which assumes fixed hardware), co-design explores the joint space of hardware configurations (SRAM size, MAC units, clock frequency, bandwidth, power budget) and model configurations (parameters, layers, activation memory). The evaluation considers compute-bound latency (limited by MAC throughput), memory-bound latency (limited by bandwidth), energy consumption (compute + memory access), and power budget constraints. The Pareto frontier identifies optimal trade-offs between latency and energy. In this mission, you implement a co-design framework that evaluates all hardware-model pairs, finds optimal configurations for different objectives (latency, energy, power), computes Pareto frontiers, and generates comprehensive co-design reports.
